messages:
lia: Hey team, customer X (private/VPC) reporting inference requests start failing ~10:15 UTC — grpc streams keep resetting. They see TLS handshake errors and our API shows 502/UNAVAILABLE.
lia: Error snippet they pasted: `rpc error: code = Unavailable desc = connection closed` and on the client side `tls: handshake failure`.
lia: They say this started after a firewall hardening change in their NACLs/security groups. Can we triage? @cheng @ingrid
sam: Thanks, lia. Can we get the control-plane logs for the failed attempts? Also ask customer for `curl --http2 -v` to our inference endpoint from a private host (not NAT gateway host) and a packet capture if possible.
lia: They ran a quick test: ``curl -v --resolve model.redwood-inference.internal:443:10.2.4.12 https://model.redwood-inference.internal/health`` returns: `* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Finished` then `* connection reset by peer` and `curl: (56) Recv failure: Connection reset by peer`.
cheng: Possible return-path ephemeral port rewrite or stateful NACL dropping related to ephemeral port range. Ask for `sudo tcpdump -n -i eth0 host 10.2.4.12 and port 443` around the repro and paste the first SYN/SYN-ACK/ACK exchange.
ingrid: Also check for TLS-inspecting appliance or inline proxy in customer's path. If they hardened SGs to allow only specific destination ports but have a proxy doing TLS terminate then reoriginate to us, mismatch of SNI/ALPN or missing cert chain could cause our runtime to close connections quickly.
lia: Customer posted tcpdump excerpt: ``10.0.5.22.52344 > 10.2.4.12.443: Flags [S], seq 0, win 64240; 10.2.4.12.443 > 10.0.5.22.52344: Flags [S.], seq 0, ack 1; 10.0.5.22.52344 > 10.2.4.12.443: Flags [R], seq 1, win 0`` — so R after SYN-ACK. They also saw `RST, ack` from 10.2.4.12 a few ms later.
sam: R after SYN-ACK means the server/app (or some middlebox) actively reset. Two hypotheses: 1) our runtime rejected the SNI/ALPN (e.g., client not sending SNI expected) and closed, 2) an inline firewall/proxy injected the R after validating client cert or other policy. Can customer try `openssl s_client -servername model.redwood-inference.internal -connect 10.2.4.12:443 -alpn h2` and paste output?
lia: They did: `CONNECTED(00000003) depth=0 CN = model.redwood-inference.internal verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate --- No peer certificate available ` then connection dropped. They also said in their NACL policy they only allow outbound ephemeral ports 32768-60999 and inbound established/related allowed.
ingrid: The verify error and "No peer certificate available" indicates the TLS handshake didn't progress to certificate send — server didn't send certificate. Could be our runtime terminating at TLS pre-cert stage due to ALPN mismatch, or a proxy doing TLS terminate and not forwarding prematch. Also check our LB health — do we have any recent autoscaling or cert rotation events? @cheng
cheng: I'm seeing a brief rollout of a cert rotation for the model endpoint at 2751231200 but it completed. No errors in control plane. However, runtime logs show `tls: client hello rejected: unsupported alpn` at 2751234505 for that customer org id. That would cause immediate R. I'll pull runtime config for that tenant.
sam: For immediate mitigation, ask customer to allow full ephemeral port range 1024-65535 temporarily and confirm no middlebox between host and our endpoint (or mirror the traffic). Also ask them to allow outbound 443 to our endpoint without TLS inspection/proxy. If they can't, we can try to accept additional ALPN variants on our side as a fallback.
lia: Customer updated NACL to 1024-65535 for outbound and customer reports streams recovered. They can reproduce failures when they revert to tightened ephemeral range. They also confirmed there was an inline DLP/proxy that was silently closing connections when ALPN didn't match expected h2 value.
ingrid: Great find. Action items: 1) support doc update with recommended ephemeral port ranges and note about inline TLS-inspection pitfalls; 2) engineering to consider more tolerant ALPN fallback for private endpoints or clearer error mapping. @cheng can you open a runtime ticket?
cheng: Will open INF-4871 with logs + repro and tag runtime and lb teams. I'll also add a small server-side telemetry change to log clearer ALPN reject reasons and include org id in the message (no PII).
lia: Thanks all — marking resolved with workaround. Customer to keep NACL widened and remove TLS-inspect proxy for now. :white_check_mark:
